newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's mobile phone system goes live.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's mobile phone system goes live.

text.p: Egypt's new mobile telephone system went live Thursday but high prices have driven away all but the affluent and the ostentatious.

The French company Alcatel has been installing a system with about 70,000 lines under a crash programme deliberately timed to give a good impression when thousands of businesspeople attend next week's Middle East economic conference.
Cartoonists have had a field day with the impact they might have on a society where it can still take several years to have a land line connected to your home or office.
Newspapers have been carrying pages of advertisements for the handsets, which are available from private retailers at about 2,000 Egyptian pounds ($590) a piece.

But the network is a monopoly of the state telephone company, which charges another 2,000 pounds ($590) to hook the subscriber up, plus a subscription of 160 pounds ($47) a month and a minimum of 60 piastres (18 cents) a minute for calls.
The company is giving priority to subscribers connected with the conference or who had applications pending to install obsolete radio phones in their cars.
The chairman of the company, the National Telecommunications Organisation (Arento), said last month he expected the number of subscribers to grow to one million in a few years.
Officials were not available on Thursday to say how many phones were working but it will be some time before they become as commonplace as they are in neighbouring Israel or Jordan.
